title: Mataya: Festival a symbol of Cultural Unity मतयाःपर्व सांस्कृतिक एकताको प्रतिक
nepali: उपत्यकाको सांस्कृतिक पर्वमध्ये ललितपुरको मतयाःपर्व विशिष्ट रहेको छ । भाद्रकृष्ण द्वितीयाका दिन मृतकको आत्माले शान्ति र निर्वाण पाउन भनी ललितपुरका बौद्ध र अन्यधार्मिक सम्पदा स्थलमा दीपयात्रा गरी मनाइने मतयाः पुराकथाको परम्परा बोकेर अघि बढेको छ । गुणकारण्डव्यूह सूत्रको चैत्य पुङ्गावदानमा उल्लेखित शशिपटनका राजा सिंहकेतुको मृत्युपश्चात् राँगोको रूपमा जन्मिएर मृत्युपछि उनको सिङको बाजाबजाइ देवस्थल परिक्रमा गरेर प्रारम्भ भएको मतयाः धार्मिक एवं सामाजिक समन्वयको प्रतिकको रूपमा लिन सकिन्छ । श्रावणशुक्लपूर्णिमाका अघिल्लो दिन कुम्भेश्वरमा नौबाजा बजाइ प्रारम्भ हुने मतयाः बौद्धकथामा आधारित भएपनि शिव र शिवगणको अनिवार्य उपस्थिति रहेको छ । मतयाःमा धार्मिक सम्पदा स्थलमा दानपारमिताको महत्व दर्शाउन दीपदानसँगै पुस्तक, विभिन्न मिठाइ र अन्य सामग्रीको दानदिने गरिन्छ । आफ्ना स्वजनको मृत्युमा मात्रै होइन अन्य जो कोही मृत्यु भएकाहरूको आत्माका शान्ति कामना गर्दै ललितपुरका चारथूर भित्रका बौद्ध सम्पदास्थल परिक्रमा गर्ने गरिन्छ । चारथूरलाई आधार मानीगरिने यस उत्सवमा जातीय भेदभाव नरहेको मतयाःलाई कुशल समाजको निर्माणको अनुपम नमूनाको रूपमा लिन सकिन्छ ।
american_english: Among the cultural festivals of the Valley, the Mataya festival of Lalitpur is distinct. Celebrated on the day of Bhadra Krishna Dwitiya with a procession of lights to Buddhist and other religious heritage sites of Lalitpur so that the souls of the deceased may attain peace and nirvana, Mataya moves forward carrying the tradition of myth. Originating from circumambulating sacred shrines while playing horn instruments made from the horns of King Simhaketu of Shashipatana—who, as mentioned in the Chaitya Pungavadana of the Gunakarandavyuha Sutra, was reborn as a water buffalo after death and died—Mataya can be taken as a symbol of religious and social harmony. Commencing on the eve of Shravana Shukla Purnima with the playing of the Naubaja at Kumbheshwar, Mataya, although based on Buddhist lore, features the mandatory presence of Shiva and the Shivagana. During Mataya, to demonstrate the importance of Dana Paramita at religious heritage sites, donations of books, various sweets, and other goods are offered alongside the donation of lamps. Circumambulating the Buddhist heritage sites within the four thurs of Lalitpur is carried out wishing peace for the souls not only upon the death of one's own relatives, but of anyone else who has died. Free of caste discrimination in this festival conducted on the basis of the four thurs, Mataya can be taken as an incomparable model for the creation of a wholesome society.

informal_english: Among the cultural festivals of the Valley, the Mataya festival of Lalitpur is quite distinct. Celebrated on the day of Bhadra Krishna Dwitiya with a procession of lights around Buddhist and other religious heritage sites of Lalitpur so departed souls can find peace and nirvana, Mataya carries on an old mythical tradition. Starting off from doing the rounds at sacred shrines while playing horn instruments made from the horns of King Simhaketu of Shashipatana—who, as noted in the Chaitya Pungavadana of the Gunakarandavyuha Sutra, came back as a water buffalo and died—Mataya can be taken as a proper symbol of religious and social harmony. Kicking off the eve of Shravana Shukla Purnima with the Naubaja being played at Kumbheshwar, Mataya, even though based on Buddhist lore, sees Shiva and his followers turning up without fail. During Mataya, to show the importance of Dana Paramita at religious heritage sites, books, all sorts of sweets, and other goodies are handed out alongside the gift of lamps. People do the rounds of the Buddhist heritage sites within the four thurs of Lalitpur wishing peace for the souls not just when their own relatives die, but for anyone who has passed away. Leaving caste discrimination out of it completely in this festival based around the four thurs, Mataya can really be taken as an unmatched example of building a proper, decent society.
